sanskrit: ya imā viśvā bhuvanāni juhvad ṛṣir hotā ny asīdat pitā naḥ | sa āśiṣā draviṇam icchamānaḥ prathamacchhad avarām̐ ā viveśa ||
english: He who sacrificed all these worlds — the seer-priest, our father — sat down as Hotṛ. Seeking wealth with his blessing, he first carved out the lower realms and entered into them.

sanskrit: kiṁ svid āsīd adhiṣṭhānam ārambhaṇaṁ katamat svit kathāsīt | yato bhūmiṁ janayan viśvakarmā vi dyām aurṇon mahinā viśvacakṣāḥ ||
english: What was the base, the point of support? What was the timber? How did it stand? From what did Viśvakarmā, the all-seeing, bring forth the earth and unfold the sky with his greatness?

sanskrit: viśvataścakṣur uta viśvatomukho viśvatobāhur uta viśvataspāt | sam bāhubhyāṁ dhamati sam patatair dyāvābhūmī janayan deva ekaḥ ||
english: He whose eyes are everywhere, whose face is everywhere, whose arms are everywhere, whose feet are everywhere — he, the one god, forging together heaven and earth with his hands and wings.

sanskrit: kiṁ svid vanaṁ ka u sa vṛkṣa āsa yato dyāvāpṛthivī niṣṭatakṣuḥ | manīṣiṇo manasā pṛcchated u tad yad adhyatiṣṭhad bhuvanāni dhārayan ||
english: What was the forest, what was the tree from which they fashioned heaven and earth? Sages enquire with the mind: upon what did he stand when he upheld the worlds?

sanskrit: yā te dhāmāni paramāṇi yāvamā yā madhyamā viśvakarmann utemā | śikṣā sakhibhyo haviṣi svadhāvaḥ svayaṁ yajasva tanvaṁ vṛdhānaḥ ||
english: Your highest abodes, O Viśvakarman, your lowest, and your middle ones as well — instruct your friends in the oblation, O Lord of self-nourishment; waxing great, sacrifice your own self.

sanskrit: viśvakarman haviṣā vāvṛdhānaḥ svayaṁ yajasva pṛthivīm uta dyām | muhyantu anye abhito janāsa ihāsmākam maghavā sūrir astu ||
english: O Viśvakarman, strengthened by the oblation, sacrifice earth and heaven yourself. Let other people about us be confounded; here let our munificent patron be the wise lord.

sanskrit: vācas patiṁ viśvakarmāṇam ūtaye manojuvaṁ vāje adyā huvema | sa no viśvāni havanāni joṣad viśvaśambhūr avase sādhukarmā ||
english: Today in the contest we call upon the Lord of Speech, Viśvakarman, swift as thought, for our aid. May he, of perfect deeds, well-being to all, be pleased with all our invocations and come to our help.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣaḥ pitā manasā hi dhīro ghṛtam ene ajanan nannamāne | yaded antā adadṛhanta pūrva ād id dyāvāpṛthivī aprathetām ||
english: The wise Father, father of the eye, gave being by his mind to these two bowing ones and kindled them with ghee. When the eastern ends were made firm, then only did heaven and earth spread out.

sanskrit: viśvakarmā vimanā ād vihāyā dhātā vidhātā paramota saṁdṛk | teṣām iṣṭāni sam iṣā madanti yatrā saptaṛṣīn para ekam āhuḥ ||
english: Viśvakarman, of surpassing mind, far-ranging, the ordainer and disposer, the highest, the all-seeing — their offerings and desires exhilarate together where they speak of the seven seers beyond the One.

sanskrit: yo naḥ pitā janitā yo vidhātā dhāmāni veda bhuvanāni viśvā | yo devānāṁ nāmadhā eka eva taṁ sampraśnam bhuvanā yanty anyā ||
english: He who is our father, our begetter and ordainer, who knows all the abodes and all the worlds, who alone assigns the names of the gods — to him the other beings come with their inquiry.

sanskrit: ta āyajanta draviṇaṁ sam asmā ṛṣayaḥ pūrve jaritāro na bhūnā | asūrte sūrte rajasi niṣatte ye bhūtāni samakṛṇvann imāni ||
english: To him the ancient seer-praisers, like heralds, sacrificed wealth together — those who sat in the unformed and formed realm of mid-air, who fashioned all these beings here.

sanskrit: paro divā para enā pṛthivyā paro devebhir asurair yad asti | kaṁ svid garbhaṁ prathamaṁ dadhra āpo yatra devāḥ samāpaśyanta viśve ||
english: Beyond the heaven, beyond this earth, beyond the gods and asuras — what was that first embryo the waters held, where all the gods gazed together?

sanskrit: tam id garbhaṁ prathamaṁ dadhra āpo yatra devāḥ samāgacchanta viśve | ajasya nābhāv adhy ekam arpitatṁ yasmin viśvāni bhuvanāni tasthuḥ ||
english: That first embryo the waters held, where all the gods came together — it is set, the One, in the navel of the Unborn, in whom all worlds stand.

sanskrit: na taṁ vidātha ya imā jajānā anyad yuṣmākam antaram babhūva | nīhāreṇa prāvṛtā jalpyā cāsutṛpa uktha śāsaś caranti ||
english: You do not know him who generated all these things — something else has come between you. Shrouded in mist, chanting emptily, those who delight in life and only proclaim hymns go their way.

sanskrit: yas te manyo 'vidhad vajra sāyaka saha ojaḥ puṣyati viśvam āṇuṣak | sāhyāma dāsam āryaṁ tvayā yujā sahaskṛtena sahasā sahasvatā ||
english: O Manyu, who aided you — the bolt, the arrow — nourishes continuous might through the whole world. With you as ally, O strength-given, violent, mighty one, may we overpower both Dāsa and Ārya.

sanskrit: manyur indro manyur evāsa devo manyur hotā varuṇo jātavedāḥ | manyuṁ viśa īḻate māṇuṣīr yāḥ pāhi no manyo tapasā sajoṣāḥ ||
english: Manyu is Indra, Manyu himself is the god; Manyu is the Hotṛ, Varuṇa, and Jātavedas. The human peoples worship Manyu. Protect us, O Manyu, united with your ardour.

sanskrit: abhīhi manyo tavasas tavīyān tapasā yujā vi jahi śatrūn | amitrahā vṛtrahā dasyuhā ca viśvā vasūny ā bharā tvaṁ naḥ ||
english: Come here, O Manyu, mightier than the mighty; with ardour as your ally, smite down our foes. Slayer of enemies, slayer of Vṛtra, slayer of Dasyus — bring all riches to us.

sanskrit: tvaṁ hi manyo abhibhūtyojāḥ svayambhūr bhāmo abhimātiṣāhaḥ | viśvacarṣaṇiḥ sahurih sahāvān asmāsv ojaḥ pṛtanāsu dhehi ||
english: For you, O Manyu, are vigour that overpowers; you are self-existent ardour, subduer of enemies; all-seeing, forceful, victorious — place your strength in us for the battles.

sanskrit: abhāgaḥ sann apa pareto asmi tava kratvā taviṣasya pracetaḥ | taṁ tvā manyo akratur jihīḻāhaṁ svā tanūr baladeyāya mehi ||
english: Portionless, I am left out, O keen-minded one — because of the intent of you, the mighty. I, O Manyu, the will-less man, have failed you; come with your own body to grant strength.

sanskrit: ayaṁ te asmy upa mehy arvāṅ pratīcīnaḥ sahure viśvadhāyaḥ | manyo vajrinn abhi mām ā vavṛtsva hanāva dasyūm̐r uta bodhy āpeḥ ||
english: I am here before you — come to me, facing me, O overpowering sustainer of all. O Manyu, wielder of the bolt, turn toward me; let us smite the Dasyus together and know yourselves allied.

sanskrit: abhi prehi dakṣiṇato bhavā me 'dhā vṛtrāṇi jaṅghanāva bhūri | juhomi te dharuṇam madhvo agram ubhā upāṁśu prathamā pibāva ||
english: Come here and stand to my right, and then together we will crush many foes. I pour for you the sweetest libation, the first drop — let us two drink together in silence.

sanskrit: tvayā manyo saratham ārujanto harṣamāṇāso dhṛṣitā marutvaḥ | tigmeṣava āyudhā saṁśiśānā abhi pra yantu naro agnirūpāḥ ||
english: O Manyu, mounting the chariot together with you, exhilarated and emboldened, the Marut-companied warriors — men of fire-like form, whetting their weapons, arrows keen — let them surge forth.

sanskrit: agnir iva manyo tviṣitaḥ sahasva senānīr naḥ sahure hūta edhi | hatvāya śatrūn vi bhajasva veda ojo mimāno vi mṛdho nudasva ||
english: Like fire, O Manyu, when kindled, overpower; be our army-leader, O overpowering one, when invoked. After slaying the enemies, divide the booty; measuring out your strength, drive away the battles.

sanskrit: sahasva manyo abhimātim asme rujan mṛṇan pramṛṇan prehi śatrūn | ugraṁ te pājo nanv ā rurudhre vaśī vaśaṁ nayasa ekaja tvam ||
english: Overpower, O Manyu, the enemy assailing us; breaking, crushing, destroying, go forth against the foes. Your fierce strength has truly advanced; you, the sole-born, bring the dependent into your power.

sanskrit: eko bahūnām asi manyav īḻito viśam-viśaṁ yudhaye saṁ śiśādhi | akṛttaruk tvayā yujā vayaṁ dyumantaṁ ghoṣaṁ vijayāya kṛṇmahe ||
english: You alone, O Manyu, are invoked by many; inspire every clan for battle. Unscathed, with you as ally, we raise the resounding battle-cry for victory.

sanskrit: vijeṣakṛd indrā ivānavabravó 'smākam manyo adhipā bhaveha | priyaṁ te nāma sahure gṛṇīmasi vidmā tam utsaṁ yata ābabhūtha ||
english: Grant us victory, irresistible like Indra; be our overlord here, O Manyu. We recite your dear name, O overpowering one; we know the source from which you arose.

sanskrit: ābhūtyā sahajā vajra sāyaka saho bibharṣy abhibhūta uttaram | kratvā no manyo saha medy edhi mahādhanasya puruhūta saṁsṛji ||
english: Born together with dominion, O bolt-like arrow, you bear a higher overpowering strength. O Manyu, by your will be united with us; O much-invoked, join us for the great prize.

sanskrit: saṁsṛṣṭaṁ dhanam ubhayaṁ samākṛtam asmabhyaṁ dattāṁ varuṇaś ca manyuḥ | bhiyaṁ dadhānā hṛdayeṣu śatavaḥ parājitāso apa ni layantām ||
english: May Varuṇa and Manyu give us both kinds of wealth, amassed and gathered together. The enemies, defeated, their hearts filled with fear, let them slink away and vanish.

sanskrit: satyenottabhitā bhūmiḥ sūryeṇottabhitā dyauḥ | ṛtenādityās tiṣṭhanti divi somo adhi śritaḥ ||
english: By truth the earth is upheld; by the sun the sky is upheld. By ṛta the Ādityas stand firm; Soma is established in heaven.

sanskrit: somenādityā balinah somena pṛthivī mahī | atho nakṣatrāṇām eṣām upasthe soma āhitaḥ ||
english: By Soma are the Ādityas mighty; by Soma the great earth stands; and in the lap of these stars here Soma is placed.

sanskrit: somam manyate papivān yat sampiṁṣanty oṣadhim | somaṁ yam brāhmaṇo vidur na tasyāśnāti kaś cana ||
english: He who drinks the pressed herb thinks he has drunk Soma. The Soma that the Brāhmaṇas know — of that no one actually partakes.

sanskrit: ācchadvidhānair gupito bārhataiḥ soma rakṣitaḥ | grāvṇām ic chṛṇvan tiṣṭhasi na te aśnāti pārthivaḥ ||
english: Shielded by covering guards, O Soma, protected by great enclosures, you stand listening to the pressing-stones; no earthly being consumes you.

sanskrit: yat tvā deva prapibanti tata ā pyāyase punaḥ | vāyuḥ somasya rakṣitā samānām māsa ākṛtiḥ ||
english: When the gods drink you fully, O god, from that you are replenished again. Vāyu is the guardian of Soma; the moon is the form of the common one.

sanskrit: raibhy āsīd anudeyī nārāśaṁsī nyocanī | sūryāyā bhadram id vāso gāthayaiti pariṣkṛtam ||
english: The Raibhī song was the accompanying gift, the Nārāśaṁsī the one that confers upon her; for Sūryā the beautiful raiment has come, adorned and completed in the hymn.

sanskrit: cittir ā upabarhaṇaṁ cakṣur ā abhyañjanam | dyaur bhūmiḥ kośa āsīd yad ayāt sūryā patim ||
english: Thought was her pillow, sight was her collyrium; heaven and earth were the casket when Sūryā went to her husband.

sanskrit: stomā āsan pratidhayaḥ kurīraṁ chanda opaśaḥ | sūryāyā aśvinā varāgnir āsīt purogavaḥ ||
english: The hymns of praise were the poles of the canopy; the metre was the bridal headgear with dangling ornaments; for Sūryā the Aśvins were the suitors; Agni was the foremost leader.

sanskrit: somo vadhūyur abhavad aśvinā stām ubhā varā | sūryāṁ yat patye śaṁsantīm manasā savitādadāt ||
english: Soma became the wooer; the Aśvins were the two suitors. When Sūryā declared herself willing in her heart, Savitṛ gave her to a husband.

sanskrit: mano asyā ana āsīd dyaur āsīd uta cchadiḥ | śukrāv anaḍvāhāv āstāṁ yad ayāt sūryā gṛham ||
english: Her mind was the cart, the sky was the canopy; the two white bullocks were yoked when Sūryā went to her new home.

sanskrit: ṛksāmābhyām abhihitau gāvau te sāmanāv itaḥ | śrotraṁ te cakre āstāṁ divi panthāś carācāraḥ ||
english: The two cows yoked by Ṛk and Sāman are your sāman-players; your two ears were the wheels; in heaven the path moves to and fro.

sanskrit: śucī te cakre yātyā vyāno akṣa āhataḥ | ano manasmayaṁ sūryārohat prayatī patim ||
english: Your two pure wheels move freely; the axle was the in-breath. Sūryā mounted the mind-made cart, going forth to her husband.

sanskrit: sūryāyā vahatuḥ prāgāt savitā yam avāsṛjat | aghāsu hanyante gāvo 'rjunayoḥ pary uhyate ||
english: The bridal procession of Sūryā went forth, which Savitṛ released. When the Maghā asterisms come, the cows are slaughtered; when the Arjunī stars come, she is driven around.

sanskrit: yad aśvinā pṛcchamānāv ayātaṁ tricakreṇa vahatuṁ sūryāyāḥ | viśve devā anu tad vām ajānan putraḥ pitarāv avṛṇīta pūṣā ||
english: When you two Aśvins came inquiring, bringing Sūryā's wedding-procession on the three-wheeled car, all the gods acknowledged that — Pūṣan, the son, chose you two as fathers.

sanskrit: yad ayātaṁ śubhas patī vareyaṁ sūryām upa | kvaika ṁ cakraṁ vām āsīt kva deṣṭrāya tasthathuḥ ||
english: When you two Lords of Beauty came to woo Sūryā — where was the one wheel of yours, and where did you two stand for the guide to the way?

sanskrit: dve te cakre sūrye brāhmaṇā ṛtuthā viduḥ | athaikaṁ cakraṁ yad guhā tad addhātaya id viduḥ ||
english: O Sūryā, the Brāhmaṇas know your two wheels according to the season. But that one hidden wheel — only the truly wise know that.

sanskrit: sūryāyai devebhyo mitrāya varuṇāya ca | ye bhūtasya pracetasa idaṁ tebhyo 'karaṁ namaḥ ||
english: To Sūryā, to the gods, to Mitra and to Varuṇa — to those who know all existing things — I have made this obeisance.

sanskrit: pūrvāparaṁ carato māyayaitau śiśū krīḻantau pari yāto adhvaram | viśvāny anyo bhuvanābhicaṣṭa ṛtūm̐r anyo vidadhaj jāyate punaḥ ||
english: These two children play and go around the sacrifice by their magic, moving forward and back. One surveys all the worlds; the other, ordained the seasons, is born again.

sanskrit: navo-navo bhavati jāyamāno 'hnāṁ ketur uṣasām ety agram | bhāgaṁ devebhyo vi dadhāty āyan pra candramās tirate dīrgham āyuḥ ||
english: Ever new he is born again; he becomes the signal of the days, going to the fore of the dawns. Coming on, he distributes the portion to the gods — the moon stretches out long life.

sanskrit: sukiṁśukaṁ śalmaliṁ viśvarūpaṁ hiraṇyavarṇaṁ suvṛtaṁ sucakram | ā roha sūrye amṛtasya lokaṁ syonam patye vahatuṁ kṛṇuṣva ||
english: Mount the car decked with kinsuka-flowers and śalmali-flowers, with all forms, gold-hued, well-turned, fair-wheeled; O Sūryā, ascend the world of immortality and make your wedding-journey pleasant for your husband.

sanskrit: ud īrṣvātaḥ pativatī hy eṣā viśvāvasum namasā gīrbhir īḻe | anyām iccha pitṛṣadaṁ vyaktām sa te bhāgo januṣā tasya viddhi ||
english: Arise hence, for this woman now has a husband. I entreat Viśvāvasu with homage and with hymns. Seek another woman not yet given in marriage, sitting with her fathers — know that to be your allotted portion from birth.

sanskrit: ud īrṣvāto viśvāvaso namasedā mahe tvā | anyām iccha prapharvyaṁ saṁ jāyām patyā sṛja ||
english: Arise hence, Viśvāvasu; with obeisance we entreat you. Seek another ripely nubile woman; release this wife to be united with her husband.

sanskrit: anṛkṣarā ṛjavaḥ santu panthā yebhiḥ sakhāyo yanti no vareyam | sam aryamā sam bhago no ninīyāt saṁ jāspatyaṁ suyamam astu devāḥ ||
english: May the paths be free of thorns, straight, by which our friends conduct our wooer. May Aryaman and Bhaga lead us together; may the conjugal bond be easily governed, O gods.

sanskrit: pra tvā muñcāmi varuṇasya pāśād yena tvābadhnāt savitā suśevaḥ ||  ṛtasya yonau sukṛtasya loke 'riṣṭāṁ tvā saha patyā dadhāmi ||
english: I free you from the bond of Varuṇa with which the auspicious Savitṛ bound you. In the womb of ṛta, in the world of good deeds, I place you unharmed together with your husband.

sanskrit: preto muñcāmi nāmutaḥ subaddhām amutas karam | yatheya indra mīḍhvaḥ suputrā subhagāsati ||
english: I release her hence, not from yonder — I make her well-bound from yonder. So that here, O Indra, bountiful god, she may be blessed with fine sons and good fortune.

sanskrit: pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinā tvā pra vahatāṁ rathena | gṛhān gaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṁ vidatham ā vadāsi ||
english: May Pūṣan lead you from here, taking you by the hand; may the Aśvins carry you onward in their chariot. Go to your home so that you may be mistress of the house; speak your will in the assembly.

sanskrit: iha priyam prajayā te sam ṛdhyatām asmin gṛhe gārhapatyāya jāgṛhi | enā patyā tanvaṁ saṁ sṛjasvādhā jivrī vidatham ā vadāthaḥ ||
english: Here may your dear happiness with offspring be fulfilled; be wakeful in this house for the gṛhapati fire. Unite your body with your husband; thus growing old together you shall speak in the assembly.

sanskrit: nīlalohitam bhavati kṛtyāsaktir vy ajyate | edhante asyā jñātayaḥ patir bandheṣu badhyate ||
english: Dark-red it becomes; the spell attached to the garment is expelled. Her kinsmen prosper; the husband is bound in bonds.

sanskrit: parā dehi śāmulyam brahmabhyo vi bhajā vasu | kṛtyaiṣā padvatī bhūtvy ā jāyā viśate patim ||
english: Give away the garment of ill omen; distribute the wealth to the Brāhmaṇas. Let this witchcraft go on its way; may the wife enter her husband as the good one.

sanskrit: aśrīrā tanūr bhavati ruśatī pāpayāmuyā | patir yad vadhvo vāsasā svam aṅgam abhidhitsate ||
english: The body becomes inauspicious, glittering and dangerous, when the husband covers his own limb with the bride's garment.

sanskrit: ye vadhvaś candraṁ vahatuṁ yakṣmā yanti janād anu | punas tān yajñiyā devā nayantu yata āgatāḥ ||
english: The diseases that follow from people to the bride's bright wedding-procession — may the sacrifice-worthy gods drive those back to where they came from.

sanskrit: mā vidan paripanthino ya āsīdanti dampatī | sugethir durgam atītāṁ apa drāntv arātayaḥ ||
english: Let not the lurkers find them, those who lie in wait for the pair of householders. May they pass through the difficult places by easy roads; let all ill-wishers flee away.

sanskrit: sumaṅgalīr iyaṁ vadhūr imāṁ sameta paśyata | saubhāgyam asyai dattvāyāthāstaṁ vi paretana ||
english: This bride is auspicious and blessed — come together and behold her. Having bestowed good fortune upon her, then go your ways home.

sanskrit: tṛṣṭam etat kaṭukam etad apāṣṭhavad viṣavan naitad attave | sūryāṁ yo brahmā vidyāt sa id vādhūyam arhati ||
english: This thing is harsh and bitter, rough and poisonous — not fit to eat. Only the Brāhmaṇa who truly knows Sūryā is worthy to conduct the wedding rites.

sanskrit: āśasanam viśasanam atho adhivikartanam | sūryāyāḥ paśya rūpāṇi tāni brahmā tu śundhati ||
english: The binding, the loosening, the cutting apart — these are the forms of Sūryā; the Brāhmaṇa purifies all these.

sanskrit: gṛbhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastam mayā patyā jaradaṣṭir yathāsaḥ | bhago aryamā savitā puraṁdhir mahyaṁ tvādur gārhapatyāya devāḥ ||
english: I take your hand for good fortune, that you may grow old with me as your husband. Bhaga, Aryaman, Savitṛ, Puraṁdhi — the gods have given you to me for the household fire.

sanskrit: tām pūṣañ chivatamām erayasva yasyām bījaṁ manuṣyā vapanti | yā na ūrū uśatī viśrayāte yasyām uśantaḥ praharāma śepam ||
english: O Pūṣan, rouse for us the most auspicious woman in whom men plant seed; who opens her thighs willingly for us; in whom we willingly deposit the phallus.

sanskrit: tubhyam agre pary avahan sūryāṁ vahatunā saha | punaḥ patibhyo jāyāṁ dā agne prajayā saha ||
english: To you first of all they led Sūryā around with the wedding-procession. O Agni, give the wife back to the husbands together with offspring.

sanskrit: punaḥ patnīm agnir adād āyuṣā saha varcasā | dīrghāyur asyā yaḥ patir jīvāti śaradaḥ śatam ||
english: Agni has given back the wife along with life and brilliance. May her husband live a long life — a hundred autumns.

sanskrit: somaḥ prathaamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ | tṛtīyo agniṣ te patis turīyas te manuṣyajāḥ ||
english: Soma first possessed you, the Gandharva possessed you next; Agni was your third husband — your fourth husband is born of men.

sanskrit: somo dadad gandharvāya gandharvo dadad agnaye | rayiṁ ca putrām̐ś cādād agnir mahyam atho imām ||
english: Soma gave to the Gandharva, the Gandharva gave to Agni; Agni gave me riches and sons, and this woman here.

sanskrit: ihaiva staṁ mā vi yauṣṭaṁ viśvam āyur vy aśnutam | krīḻantau putrair naptṛbhir modamānau sve gṛhe ||
english: Be here; do not be parted from each other; live out your full span of life. Sporting with your sons and grandsons, rejoicing in your own home.

sanskrit: ā naḥ prajāṁ janayatu prajāpatir ājarasāya sam anaktv aryamā | adurmaṅgalīḥ patilokam ā viśa śaṁ no bhava dvipade śaṁ catuṣpade ||
english: May Prajāpati generate offspring for us; may Aryaman anoint us for old age together. O you who are of good omen, enter your husband's world; be auspicious to us among bipeds and quadrupeds.

sanskrit: aghora cakṣur apatighny edhi śivā paśubhyaḥ sumanāḥ suvarcāḥ | vīrasūr devakāmā syonā śaṁ no bhava dvipade śaṁ catuṣpade ||
english: Be of gentle gaze, no slayer of your husband; be kind to our cattle, of good mind, of good splendour; bearing heroes, devoted to the gods, gentle — be auspicious to us among bipeds and quadrupeds.

sanskrit: imāṁ tvam indra mīḍhvaḥ suputrāṁ subhagāṁ kṛṇu | daśāsyām putrān ā dhehi patim ekādaśaṁ kṛdhi ||
english: O bountiful Indra, make this woman blessed with fine sons and good fortune. Place ten sons in her and make the husband the eleventh.

sanskrit: samrājñī śvaśure bhava samrājñī śvaśrvām bhava | nanāndari samrājñī bhava samrājñī adhi devṛṣu ||
english: Be a queen before your father-in-law; be a queen before your mother-in-law. Be a queen before your husband's sister; be a queen before your husband's brothers.

sanskrit: sam añjantu viśve devāḥ sam āpo hṛdayāni nau | sam mātariśvā saṁ dhātā sam u deṣṭrī dadhātu nau ||
english: May all the gods unite our hearts; may the waters unite our hearts. May Mātariśvan, may Dhātṛ, may Deṣṭrī join our two hearts together.

sanskrit: vi hi sotor asṛkṣata nendraṁ devam amaṁsata | yatrāmadad vṛṣākapir aryaḥ puṣṭeṣu matsakkhā viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: The soma-pressers flowed forth; they did not honour Indra as god, where Vṛṣākapi, the noble one, made merry in prosperity — my companion. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: parā hy indra dhāvasi vṛṣākaiper ati vyathiḥ | no aha pra vindasy anyatra somapītaye viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: You run away, O Indra, beyond Vṛṣākapi's trouble. You find nothing elsewhere for the drinking of Soma. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: kim ayaṁ tvāṁ vṛṣākapiś cakāra harito mṛgaḥ | yasmā irasyasīd u nv aryo vā puṣṭimad vasu viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: What has this tawny beast Vṛṣākapi done to you, that you are angry at him, O nobleman, because of his prosperous goods? Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: yam imaṁ tvaṁ vṛṣākapim priyam indrābhirakṣasi | śvā nv asya jambhiṣad api karṇe varāhayur viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: This Vṛṣākapi whom you cherish, O Indra, whom you protect as your favourite — a dog that is boar-hunting will snap at his ear. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: priyā taṣṭāni me kaapir vyaktā vy adūduṣat | śiro nv asya rāviṣaṁ na sugaṁ duṣkṛte bhuvam viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: The ape has damaged my carved, manifest, precious things. I would cut off his head — it would go ill for the evil-doer. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: na mat strī subhasattarā na suyāśutarā bhuvat | na mat praticyavīyasī na sakthy udyamīyasī viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: No woman sits in a better seat than I; no woman is swifter in the race than I; none is more forward than I; none lifts her thighs higher than I. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: uve amba sulābhike yathevāṅga bhaviṣyati | bhasaṇ me amba sakthi me śiro me vīva hṛṣyati viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: Yes, dear easily-found mother, it shall be just as you say. My rump, my thigh, my head — I am excited all over. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: kiṁ subāho svaṅgure pṛthuṣṭo pṛthujāghane | kiṁ śūrapatni nas tvam abhy amīṣi vṛṣākapiṁ viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: Why, O fair-armed, pretty-fingered, broad-hipped, wide-thighed one — why do you, O wife of the hero, cast hostile glances at our Vṛṣākapi? Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: avīrām iva mām ayaṁ śarārur abhi manyate | utāham asmi vīriṇīndrapatnī marutsakhā viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: This scoundrel thinks of me as if I were without a husband. But I am indeed the heroic wife of Indra, companion of the Maruts. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: saṁhotraṁ sma purā nārī samanam vāva gacchati | vedhā ṛtasya vīriṇīndrapatnī mahīyate viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: In former times the woman went indeed to the assembly and to the joint invocation. The creative heroine, follower of ṛta, the wife of Indra, is exalted. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: indrāṇīm āsu nāriṣu subhagām aham aśravam | na hy asyā aparam cana jarasā marate patir viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: I have heard that Indrāṇī is the most blessed among these women — for her husband never dies of old age. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: nāham indrāṇi rāraṇa sakhyur vṛṣākaiper ṛte | yasyedam apyaṁ haviḥ priyaṁ devesṣu gacchati viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: I, Indrāṇī, would not rejoice without my companion Vṛṣākapi, whose dear, moist oblation goes among the gods. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: vṛṣākapāyi revati suputra ād u susnuṣe | ghasat ta indra ukṣaṇaḥ priyaṁ kācitkaraṁ havir viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: O wealthy wife of Vṛṣākapi, blessed with fine sons and fine daughters-in-law — may Indra eat the bulls for you, the dear offering that brings fulfilment. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: ukṣṇo hi me pañcadaśa sākam pacanti viṁśatim | utāham admi pīva id ubhā kukṣī pṛṇanti me viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: For me they cook fifteen and twenty bulls at once. I eat the fat and both my flanks are filled. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: vṛṣabho na tigmaśṛṅgo 'ntar yūtheṣu rorurvat | manthas ta indra śaṁ hṛde yaṁ te sunoti bhāvayur viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: Like a sharp-horned bull roaring among the herds — O Indra, the pressed draught pleases your heart, which the devoted presser presses for you. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: na seśe yasya rambate 'ntarā sakthyā kapṛt | sed īśe yasya romaśaṁ niṣeduṣo vijṛmbhate viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: He does not prevail in whose thighs the penis dangles. He prevails whose hairy thing opens wide when he sits down. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: na seśe yasya romaśaṁ niṣeduṣo vijṛmbhate | sed īśe yasya rambate 'ntarā sakthyā kapṛd viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: He does not prevail whose hairy thing opens wide when he sits down. He prevails in whose thighs the penis dangles. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: ayam indra vṛṣākapiḥ parasvantaṁ hataṁ vidat | asiṁ sūnāṁ navaṁ carum ād edhasya āna ācitaṁ viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: This Vṛṣākapi, O Indra, has found the slain enemy's wealth: a sword, a new meat-cooking pot, loaded with firewood. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: ayam emi vicākaśad vicinvan dāsam āryam | pibāmi pākasutvanno 'bhi dhīram acākaśam viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: I go about observing clearly, distinguishing the Dāsa from the Ārya. I drink of the simple presser's draught, gazing upon the wise one. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: dhanva ca yat kṛntaṭraṁ ca kati svit tā vi yojanā | nedīyaso vṛṣākape 'stam ehi gṛhām̐ upa viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: The desert and the cutting-forest — how many leagues separate them? O Vṛṣākapi, come homeward, come back to the nearer dwellings. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: punar ehi vṛṣākape suvitā kalpayāvahai | ya eṣa svapnanāṁśano 'stam eṣi pathā punar viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: Come back again, Vṛṣākapi; let us two arrange things well. You who destroy sleep, come back by the path to the home. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: yad udañco vṛṣākape gṛham indrājagantana | kva sya pulvagho mṛgaḥ kam agañ janayopano viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: When you two came home northward, O Indra and Vṛṣākapi — where has that nimble beast gone, who pleased the people of the house? Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: parśur ha nāma mānavī sākaṁ sasūva viṁśatim | bhadraṁ bhala tyasyā abhūd yasyā udaram āmayad viśvasmād indra uttaraḥ ||
english: Parśu, a human woman, bore twenty children at one time. Good fortune came indeed to her whose belly bore this pain. Indra is above all things.

sanskrit: rakṣohaṇaṁ vājinam ā jigharmi mitram prathiṣṭham upa yāmi śarma | śiśāno agniḥ kratubhiḥ samiddhaḥ sa no divā sa riṣaḥ pātu naktam ||
english: I kindle the demon-slaying, powerful Agni; I approach the protection of the most widely renowned friend. Agni, whetted and kindled with sacred rites — may he guard us by day and guard us by night from harm.

sanskrit: ayodaṁṣṭro arciṣā yātudhānān upa spṛśa jātavedaḥ samiddhaḥ | ā jihvayā mūradevān rabhasva kravyādo vṛktvā api dhatsv āsan ||
english: O Jātavedas, kindled, with your iron fangs touch the Yātudhānas with your flame. With your tongue seize upon the wicked gods; having cut down the flesh-eaters, place them in your mouth.

sanskrit: ubhobhayāvinn upa dhehi daṁṣṭrā hiṁsraḥ śiśāno 'varam paraṁ ca | utāntarikṣe pari yāhi rājan jambhaiḥ saṁ dhehy abhi yātudhānān ||
english: Set your two deadly fangs, biting both from below and above, O king. And circling through the atmosphere, crush the Yātudhānas with your jaws.

sanskrit: yajñair iṣūḥ saṁnamamāno agne vācā śalyām̐ aśanibhir dihānaḥ | tābhir vidhya hṛdaye yātudhānān pratīco bāhūn prati bhaṅdhy eṣām ||
english: O Agni, having bent your arrows with sacrifices, smearing the sticks with your voice like lightning-bolts — with these pierce the Yātudhānas in the heart; break the backs of their arms.

sanskrit: agne tvacaṁ yātudhānasya bhindhi hiṁsrāśanir harasā hantv enam | pra parvāṇi jātavedaḥ śṛṇīhi kravyāt kraviṣṇur vi cinotu vṛkṇam ||
english: O Agni, split the skin of the Yātudhāna; your flame like a deadly bolt should smite him. O Jātavedas, shatter his limbs joint by joint; let the flesh-rending flesh-devourer scatter the shreds.

sanskrit: yatreidānīm paśyasi jātavedas tiṣṭhantam agna uta vā carantam | yad vāntarikṣe pathibhiḥ patantaṁ tam astā vidhya śarvā śiśānaḥ ||
english: Where now you see him, O Jātavedas, standing or moving, or flying through the atmosphere on its pathways — with your whetted arrow shoot him, O Śarva.

sanskrit: utālabdhaṁ spṛṇuhi jātaveda ālebhānād ṛṣṭibhir yātudhānāt | agne pūrvo ni jahi śośucāna āmādaḥ kṣviṅkās tam adantv enīḥ ||
english: Deliver also the one who has been caught, O Jātavedas, from the Yātudhāna that has seized upon him. O Agni, blazing, strike down the attacker first; let the spotted ewes that devour raw flesh eat him.

sanskrit: iha pra brūhi yatamaḥ so agne yo yātudhāno ya idaṁ kṛṇoti | tam ā rabhasva samidhā yaviṣṭha nṛcakṣasaś cakṣuṣe randhayainam ||
english: Declare here which one it is, O Agni — which Yātudhāna is doing this thing. Seize him with your faggot, O youngest one; deliver him to the sight of the man-seeing one.

sanskrit: tīkṣṇenāgne cakṣuṣā rakṣa yajñam prāñcaṁ vasubhyaḥ pra ṇaya pracetaḥ | hiṁsraṁ rakṣāṁsy abhi śośucānam mā tvā dabhan yātudhānā nṛcakṣaḥ ||
english: With your sharp eye guard the sacrifice, O Agni; lead it forward to the Vasus, O wise one. Blazing against the injurious demons — let not the Yātudhānas deceive you, O man-seeing one.

sanskrit: nṛcakṣā rakṣaḥ pari paśya vikṣu tasya trīṇi prati śṛṇīhy agrā | tasyāgne pṛṣṭīr harasā śṛṇīhi tredhā mūlaṁ yātudhānasya vṛśca ||
english: O man-seeing one, scan the demon about the settlements; shatter the three points of his weapon. O Agni, shear his ribs with your heat; cut the Yātudhāna's root in three places.

sanskrit: trir yātudhānaḥ prasitiṁ ta etv ṛtaṁ yo agne anṛtena hanti | tam arciṣā sphūrjayan jātavedaḥ samakṣam enaṁ gṛṇate ni vṛṅdhi ||
english: Let the Yātudhāna come thrice into your snare — whoever, O Agni, attacks truth with falsehood. Thundering with your flame, O Jātavedas, destroy him openly before the one who praises you.

sanskrit: tad agne cakṣuḥ prati dhehi rebhe śaphārujam yena paśyasi yātudhānam | atharvaavaj jyotiṣā daivyena satyaṁ dhūrvantam acitaṁ ny oṣa ||
english: O Agni, set your eye — the hoof-breaking, revealing eye — with which you see the Yātudhāna. Like Atharvan, with the divine light, burn up the unrecognised one who injures truth.

sanskrit: yad agne adya mithunā śapāto yad vācas tṛṣṭaṁ janayanta rebhāḥ | manyor manasaḥ śaravyā jāyate yā tayā vidhya hṛdaye yātudhānān ||
english: O Agni, the arrow that is born from the biting of pairs this day, when the chanting ones produce the harsh weapon of voice from wrath of mind — with that arrow pierce the Yātudhānas in the heart.

sanskrit: parā śṛṇīhi tapasā yātudhānān parāgne rakṣo harasā śṛṇīhi | parārciṣā mūradevāñ chṛṇīhi parāsutṛpo abhi śośucānaḥ ||
english: O Agni, sever the Yātudhānas with your heat; sever the demons with your flame. Blazing, sever the wicked gods with your rays; sever the devourers of life.

sanskrit: parādya devā vṛjinaṁ śṛṇantu pratyag enaṁ śapathā yantu tṛṣṭāḥ ||  vācāstenaṁ śarava ṛcchantu marman viśvasyaitu prasitiṁ yātudhānaḥ ||
english: Today let the gods cut away the crooked one; let the fierce curses turn back upon him. Let the arrows of speech reach the vital spot of the word-thief; let the Yātudhāna come to the snare of all.

sanskrit: yaḥ pauruṣeyeṇa kraviṣā samaṅkte yo aśvyena paśunā yātudhānaḥ | yo aghnyāyā bharati kṣīram agne teṣāṁ śīrṣāṇi harasāpi vṛśca ||
english: The Yātudhāna who compounds himself with human flesh, with horse-flesh, with cattle-flesh; who steals the milk of the unwounded cow — O Agni, cut off their heads with your flame.

sanskrit: saṁvatsarīṇam paya usriyāyās tasya māśīd yātudhāno nṛcakṣaḥ | pīyūṣam agne yatamas titṛpsāt tam pratyañcam arciṣā vidhya marman ||
english: Let the Yātudhāna not eat the year-long milk of the cow, O man-seeing one. O Agni, whichever one would swallow the colostrum — pierce that one straight through the vitals with your flame.

sanskrit: viṣam gavāṁ yātudhānāḥ pibantv ā vṛścyantām aditaye durevāḥ | parainān devaḥ savitā dadātu parā bhāgam oṣadhīnāṁ jayantām ||
english: Let the Yātudhānas drink the poison of the cows; let the evil-fated ones be cut off for Aditi. Let the god Savitṛ deliver them away; let them win away their portion from the plants.

sanskrit: sanād agne mṛṇasi yātudhānān na tvā rakṣāṁsi pṛtanāsu jigyuḥ | anu daha sahamūrān kravyādo mā te hetyā mukṣata daivyāyāḥ ||
english: From of old, O Agni, you have slain the Yātudhānas; the demons have not overcome you in battles. Burn the flesh-eating fools one after another; let them not escape your divine weapon.

sanskrit: tvaṁ no agne adharād udaktāt tvam paścād uta rakṣā purastāt | preti te te ajarāsas tapiṣṭhā aghaśaṁsaṁ śośucato dahantu ||
english: O Agni, protect us from below and above, from behind, and guard us from the front as well. Let your ageless, most burning ones, blazing, burn up the evil-speaker.

sanskrit: paścāt purastād adharād udaktāt kaviḥ kāvyena pari pāhi rājan | sakhe sakhāyam ajaro jariṁṇe 'gne martām̐ amartyas tvaṁ naḥ ||
english: O king, guard us from behind and in front, from below and above, O seer, with your poet-wisdom. O Agni, friend to the friend, ageless against decay, immortal among us mortals.

sanskrit: pari tvāgne puraṁ vayaṁ vipraṁ sahasya dhīmahi | dhṛṣadvarnạṁ dive-dive hantāram bhaṅgurāvatām ||
english: O Agni, we set you as a rampart of strength around us — the inspired one, bright-hued day by day, slayer of those who are crooked of will.

sanskrit: viṣeṇa bhaṅgurāvataḥ prati ṣma rakṣaso daha | agne tigmena śociṣā tapuragrābhir ṛṣṭibhi ||
english: With poison burn back the crooked-willed demons, O Agni, with your sharp flame, with your heat-tipped spears.

sanskrit: praty agne mithunā daha yātudhānā kimīdinā | saṁ tvā śiśāmi jāgṛhy adabdhaṁ vipra manmabhiḥ ||
english: O Agni, burn back the paired Yātudhānas, the Kimīdins. I sharpen you; be undeceived and wakeful, O inspired one, with sacred thoughts.

sanskrit: praty agne harasā haraḥ śṛṇīhi viśvataḥ prati | yātudhānasya rakṣaso balaṁ vi ruja vīryam ||
english: O Agni, with your heat shear back the heat; sever it on all sides. Break the force and heroic strength of the Yātudhāna demon.

sanskrit: haviṣ pāntam ajaraṁ svarvidi diviSpṛśy āhutaṁ juṣṭam agnau | tasya bharmaṇe bhuvanāya devā dharmaṇe kam svadhayā paprathanta ||
english: The oblation protected, ageless, heaven-finding, touching the sky, offered and accepted in the fire — for the bearing of that, for the world, for the law, the gods spread out with their self-power.

sanskrit: gīrṇam bhuvanaṁ tamasāpagūḷham āviḥ svar abhavaj jāte agnau | tasya devāḥ pṛthivī dyaur utāpo 'raṇayann oṣadhīḥ sakhye asya ||
english: The world swallowed, hidden by darkness, became manifest in light when Agni was born. At his birth the gods — earth, sky, waters — and the plants rejoiced in his friendship.

sanskrit: devebhir nv iṣito yajñiyebhir agniṁ stoṣāṇy ajaram bṛhantam | yo bhānunā pṛthivīṁ dyām utaemām ātātatana rodasī antarikṣam ||
english: Urged on by the sacrifice-worthy gods, I will now praise Agni, the ageless, the great — he who with his radiance stretched out earth, this sky here, and the two worlds, and the atmosphere.

sanskrit: yo hotāsīt prathamo devajuṣṭo yaṁ samāñjann ājyenā vṛṇānāḥ | sa patatrītvaram sthā jagad yac chvātram agnir akṛṇoj jātavedaḥ ||
english: He who was the first Hotṛ, dear to the gods, whom they anointed with ghee as they chose him — Agni Jātavedas made swift both the winged world and the four-footed world.

sanskrit: yaj jātavedo bhuvanasya mūrdhann atiṣṭho agne saha rocanena | taṁ tvāhema matibhir gīrbhir ukthaiḥ sa yajñiyo abhavo rodasiprāḥ ||
english: O Jātavedas, O Agni, when you stood at the top of the world with the shining realm — we praise you with thoughts, hymns, and recitations. Thus you became worthy of sacrifice, filling the two worlds.

sanskrit: mūrdhā bhuvo bhavati naktam agnis tataḥ sūryo jāyate prātar udyan | māyām ū tu yajñiyānām etām apo yat tūrṇiś carati prajānan ||
english: Agni becomes the crown of the earth by night; from that the sun is born, rising at dawn. This is the power of those worthy of sacrifice: the water moves swiftly with full understanding.

sanskrit: dṛśenyo yo mahinā samiddho 'rocata diviyonir vibhāvā | tasminn agnau sūktavākena devā havir viśva ājuhavus tanūpāḥ ||
english: He who, sky-born, blazing with greatness, shone brilliantly and was worth beholding — into that Agni the self-sustaining gods poured all oblations with the words of the well-spoken hymn.

sanskrit: sūktavākam prathamam ād id agnim ād id havir ajanayanta devāḥ | sa eṣāṁ yajño abhavat tanūpās taṁ dyaur veda tam pṛthivī tam āpaḥ ||
english: First and foremost the gods generated the well-spoken hymn, and then Agni, and then the oblation. He became their self-sustaining sacrifice — sky knows him, earth knows him, the waters know him.

sanskrit: yaṁ devāso 'janayantāgniṁ yasminn ājuhavur bhuvanāni viśvā | so arciṣā pṛthivīṁ dyām utaemām ṛjūyamāno atapan mahitvā ||
english: The Agni whom the gods generated, into whom they poured all the worlds — he, straightening out with his flame both earth and this sky, warmed them with his greatness.

sanskrit: stomena hi divi devāso agnim ajījanañ chakti bhī rodasiprām | tam ū akṛṇvan tredhā bhuve kaṁ sa oṣadhīḥ pacati viśvarūpāḥ ||
english: For with praise the gods in heaven generated Agni, filling the two worlds with his powers. They made him threefold for the world — he cooks the plants of all forms.

sanskrit: yaded enam adadhur yajñiyāso divi devāḥ sūryam āditeiyam | yadā cariṣṇū mithunāv abhūtām ād it prāpaśyan bhuvanāni viśvā ||
english: When the sacrifice-worthy gods placed him in heaven as the solar child of Aditi — when the two moving ones became a pair, then all the worlds saw everything.

sanskrit: viśvasmā agnim bhuvanāya devā vaiśvānaram ketum ahnām akṛṇvan | ā yas tatānoṣaso vibhātīr apo ūrṇoti tamo arciṣā yan ||
english: For the good of all the world the gods made Agni Vaiśvānara the signal light of days — he who stretches out the shining dawns and removes darkness, going with his flame.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaram kavayo yajñiyāso 'gniṁ devā ajanayann ajuryam | nakṣatram pratnam aminac cariṣṇu yakṣasyādhyakṣaṁ taviṣam bṛhantam ||
english: The poet-seers, the sacrifice-worthy gods, generated Agni Vaiśvānara as the imperishable; he who moved, shaking the ancient star — the mighty, great overseer of the sacrifice.

sanskrit: vaiśvānaram viśvahā dīdivāṁsam mantrair agniṁ kavim acchā vadāmaḥ | yo mahimnā paribabhūvorvī utāvastād uta devaḥ parastāt ||
english: We address with sacred hymns Agni the wise, Vaiśvānara, ever blazing — he who by his greatness encompassed the wide earth, god from below and from above.

sanskrit: dve srutī aśṛṇavam pitṝṇām ahaṁ devānām uta martyānām | tābhyām idaṁ viśvam ejat sam eti yad antarā pitaram mātaraṁ ca ||
english: I have heard of two paths — of the Fathers and of the gods — and of mortals. By these two paths all this moving world comes together, whatever is between Father Heaven and Mother Earth.

sanskrit: dve samīcī bibhṛtaś carantaṁ śīrṣato jātam manasā vimṛṣṭam | sa pratyaṅ viśvā bhuvanāni tasthāv aprayucchan taraṇir bhrājamānaḥ ||
english: The two that embrace each other carry him who moves, born from the head, comprehended by the mind. He has stood facing all the worlds, without faltering, the swift one, blazing.

sanskrit: yatrā vadete avaraḥ paraś ca yajnanyoḥ kataro nau vi veda | ā śekur it sadhamādaṁ sakhāyo nakṣanta yajñaṁ ka idaṁ vi vocat ||
english: Where the lower and the upper speak, of the two sacrificial ones — which one of us two does he know? Friends have reached the common banquet; who can proclaim this sacrifice?

sanskrit: katy agnayaḥ kati sūryāsaḥ katy uṣāsaḥ katy u svid āpaḥ | nopaspijam vaḥ pitaro vadāmi pṛcchāmi vaḥ kavayo vidmane kam ||
english: How many fires, how many suns, how many dawns, how many waters are there? I am not speaking controversially to you, O Fathers — I am asking you, O sages, to know.

sanskrit: yāvanmātram uṣaso na pratīkaṁ suparṇyo vasate mātariśvaḥ | tāvad dadhāty upa yajñam āyan brāhmaṇo hotur avaro niṣīdan ||
english: For as great a measure as the face of the dawn in which the eagle Mātariśvan dwells — to that measure the Brāhmaṇa who comes to the sacrifice, sitting below the Hotṛ, establishes it.

sanskrit: indraṁ stavā nṛtamaṁ yasya mahnā vibabādhe rocanā vi jmo antān | ā yaḥ paprau carṣaṇīdhṛd varobhiḥ pra sindhubhyo riricāno mahitvā ||
english: I praise Indra the most manly, by whose greatness the shining realms and the ends of the earth were pushed apart — he who, holding men together, filled the wide spaces, overflowing with his greatness beyond the rivers.

sanskrit: sa sūryaḥ pary urū varāṁsy endro vavṛtyād rathyeva cakrā | atiṣṭhantam apasyam na sargaṁ kṛṣṇā tamāṁsi tviṣyā jaghāna ||
english: Indra turned the sun around the wide dwelling places like chariot wheels. He smote the dark darkneses with his brilliance, like a flood that stays nothing.

sanskrit: samānam asmā anapāvṛd arca kṣmayā divo asamamm brahma navyam | vi yaḥ pṛṣṭheva janimāny arya indraś cikāya na sakhāyam īṣe ||
english: Chant for him the unceasing, unturning hymn — the new prayer unlike any in earth or sky. Indra, the noble one, sorted out the births like backs of cattle; he does not rule over a friend.

sanskrit: indrāya giro aniśitasargā apaḥ preyayaṁ sagarasya budhnāt | yo akṣeṇeva cakriyā śacībhir viṣvak tastambha pṛthivīm uta dyām ||
english: I send forth songs to Indra like an unrestricted current of waters from the depth of the ocean — he who, like an axle-pin holding the wheels, with his powers propped apart earth and heaven on every side.

sanskrit: āpāntamanyus tṛpalaprabharmā dhuni śimīvāñ charumām̐ ṛjīṣī | somo viśvāny atasā vanāni nārvāg indram pratimānāni debhuḥ ||
english: His anger has drunk its fill; with triple food he has been nourished; he is the rushing, laborious one, with mace, the soma-drinker. The stalky shrubs and forests — none of the things below have deceived Indra.

sanskrit: na yasya dyāvāpṛthivī na dhanva nāntarikṣaṁ nādrayaḥ somo akṣāḥ | yad asya manyor adhinīyamānaḥ śṛṇāti vīḻu rujati sthirāṇi ||
english: Neither heaven and earth, nor desert, nor atmosphere, nor mountains, nor Soma have measured him. When his wrath is stirred, he shatters the solid and breaks the firm things.

sanskrit: jaghāna vṛtraṁ svadhitir vanevā ruroja puro arada na sindhūn | bibheda girim avam in na kumbham ā gā indro akṛṇuta svayugbhiḥ ||
english: He slew Vṛtra like an axe in the forest; he broke the strongholds and dug out the rivers. He split the mountain like a new water jar; Indra freed the cows with his own yoke-fellows.

sanskrit: tvaṁ ha tyad ṛṇayā indra dhīro 'sir na parva vṛjinā śṛṇāsi | pra ye mitrasya varuṇasya dhāma yujam na janā minanti mitram ||
english: You, O Indra the wise, cut off that sin-incurring thing; like a sword you sever crooked limb from limb. Those who injure the law of Mitra and Varuṇa injure a friend, as if breaking a yoke-fellow.

sanskrit: pra ye mitram prāryamaṇaṁ durevāḥ pra saṁgirah pra varuṇam minanti | ny amitrreṣu vadham indra tumram vṛṣan vṛṣāṇam aruṣam śiśīhi ||
english: Those evil ones who injure Mitra, who injure Aryaman, who injure the compacts, who injure Varuṇa — sharpen your heavy weapon against the enemies, O bull, the red-rayed one that whets itself.

sanskrit: indro diva indra īśe pṛthivyā indro apām indra it parvatānām | indro vṛdhām indra in medhirāṇām indraḥ kṣeme yoge havya indraḥ ||
english: Indra is lord of heaven; Indra is lord of earth; Indra is lord of the waters, of the mountains. Indra is lord of the prosperous, lord of the wise; Indra is to be invoked in peace and in toil.

sanskrit: prāktubhya indraḥ pra vṛdho ahabhyaḥ prāntarikṣāt pra samudrasya dhāseḥ | pra vātasya prathasaḥ pra jmo antāt pra sindhubhyo ririce pra kṣitibhyaḥ ||
english: Indra excels the seasons, the days; he excels the atmosphere, the lap of the ocean. He excels the breadth of the wind, the ends of the earth; he overflows beyond the rivers and the dwelling-places.

sanskrit: pra śośucatyā uṣaso na ketur asivā te vartatām indra hetiḥ | aśmeva vidhya diva ā sṛjānas tapiṣṭhena heṣasā droghamitrān ||
english: Like a blazing signal of the dawns, may your weapon revolve, O Indra, unhindered. Piercing like a stone, hurled down from heaven — with your most burning weapon strike those who are false friends.

sanskrit: anv aha māsā anv id vanāny anv oṣadhīr anu parvatāsaḥ | anv indraṁ rodasī vāvaśāne anv āpo ajihata jāyamānam ||
english: The months followed him, the forests followed him, the plants followed him, the mountains followed him. The two worlds crying out followed Indra; the waters followed him as he was born.

sanskrit: karhi svit sā ta indra cetyāsad aghasya yad bhinado rakṣa eṣat | mitraakruvo yac chasane na gāvaḥ pṛthivyā āpṛg amuyā śayante ||
english: When, O Indra, will that be perceived of you — that you struck the demon that was destroying the wicked? Those who are hostile to Mitra, like cattle at the slaughtering post — when will they lie fallen, stuck to this earth?

sanskrit: śatrūyanto abhi ye nas tataste mahi vrādhanta ogaṇāsaa indra | andhenāmitrās tamasā sacantāṁ sujyotiṣo aktavas tāṁ abhi ṣyuḥ ||
english: Those hostile enemies that have crept upon us, who swelled as a mighty army — O Indra, let the enemies be engulfed in blind darkness; may the nights rich in good light pour over them.

sanskrit: purūṇi hi tvā savanā janānām brahmāṇi mandan gṛṇatām ṛṣīṇām | imām āghoṣann avasā sahūtiṁ tiro viśvām̐ arcato yāhy arvāṅ ||
english: Truly, many a pressing-rite of peoples exhilarates you; the prayers of the singing seers exhilarate you. Resounding here with help and companioned invocation, pass beyond all who sing hymns and come to us.

sanskrit: evā te vayam indra bhuñjatīnāṁ vidyāma sumatīnāṁ navānām | vidyāma vastor avasā gṛṇanto viśvāmitrā uta ta indra nūnam ||
english: Thus may we, O Indra, know you to be of those who enjoy, of those who are newly benevolent. Praising, may we know you at the turning of each day with your help; we are Viśvāmitras, O Indra, even now.

sanskrit: śunaṁ huvema maghavānam indram asmin bhare nṛtamaṁ vājasātau | śṛṇvantam ugram ūtaye samatsu ghantaṁ vṛtrāṇi saṁjitaṁ dhanānām ||
english: For our welfare may we call upon Maghavan Indra, the most manly in this battle for the prize — the fierce one who hearkens for our aid in conflicts, smiting Vṛtras, conqueror of wealth.

sanskrit: sahasraśīrṣā puruṣaḥ sahasrākṣaḥ sahasrapāt | sa bhūmiṁ viśvato vṛtvāty atiṣṭhad daśāṅgulam ||
english: The Puruṣa has a thousand heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet. He surrounds the earth on all sides and extends beyond by ten fingers.

sanskrit: puruṣa evedaṁ sarvaṁ yad bhūtaṁ yac ca bhavyam | utāmṛtatvasyeśāno yad annenātirohati ||
english: This Puruṣa is indeed all this world — what has been and what shall be. And he is lord of immortality, that which grows beyond through food.

sanskrit: etāvān asya mahimāto jyāyāṁś ca pūruṣaḥ | pādo 'sya viśvā bhūtāni tripād asyāmṛtaṁ divi ||
english: Such is his greatness, yet Puruṣa is greater still. One quarter of him is all living beings here; three quarters of him are the immortal in heaven.

sanskrit: tripād ūrdhva ud ait puruṣaḥ pādo 'syehābhavat punaḥ | tato viṣvaṅ vy akrāmat sāśanānaśane abhi ||
english: Three quarters of the Puruṣa rose upward; one quarter here came into being again. From that he stepped forward on all sides, into what eats and what does not eat.

sanskrit: tasmād virāḷ ajāyata virājo adhi pūruṣaḥ | sa jāto aty aricyata paścād bhūmim atho puraḥ ||
english: From him Virāj was born; from Virāj the Puruṣa was born again. Being born, he extended beyond the earth — both behind and before.

sanskrit: yat puruṣeṇa haviṣā devā yajñam atanvata | vasanto asyāsīd ājyaṁ grīṣma idhmaḥ śarad dhaviḥ ||
english: When the gods, with the Puruṣa as their oblation, spread out the sacrifice — spring was the melted butter, summer was the firewood, and autumn was the offering.

sanskrit: taṁ yajñam barhaṣi praukṣan puruṣaṁ jātam agrataḥ | tena devā ayajanta sādhyā ṛṣayaś ca ye ||
english: They consecrated with water on the barhis-grass the Puruṣa born in the beginning. With him the gods sacrificed, and the Sādhyas, and the seers.

sanskrit: tasmād yajñāt sarvahutaḥ sambhṛtaṁ pṛṣadājyam | paśūn tāṁś cakre vāyavyān āraṇyān grāmyāś ca ye ||
english: From that sacrifice in which everything was offered, the clotted oblation was gathered. He made from it the animals of the air — those of the forest and those of the village.

sanskrit: tasmād yajñāt sarvahuta ṛcaḥ sāmāni jajñire | chandāṁsi jajñire tasmād yajus tasmād ajāyata ||
english: From that all-offered sacrifice were born the Ṛk-verses and the Sāmans. The metres were born from it; the Yajus was born from it.

sanskrit: tasmād aśvā ajāyanta ye ke cobhayādataḥ | gāvo ha jajñire tasmāt tasmāj jātā ajāvayaḥ ||
english: From it were born horses, and all creatures with two rows of teeth. Cows were born from it; from it were born goats and sheep.

sanskrit: yat puruṣaṁ vy adadhuḥ katidhā vy akalpayan | mukhaṁ kim asya kau bāhū kā ūrū pādā ucyete ||
english: When they divided the Puruṣa, into how many parts did they arrange him? What is his mouth called? What his two arms? What are his two thighs and his two feet called?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo 'sya mukham āsīd bāhū rājanyaḥ kṛtaḥ | ūrū tad asya yad vaiśyaḥ padbhyāṁ śūdro ajāyata ||
english: His mouth was the Brāhmaṇa; his two arms were made the Rājanya; his two thighs are what the Vaiśya is; from his two feet the Śūdra was born.

sanskrit: candramā manaso jātaś cakṣoḥ sūryo ajāyata | mukhād indraś cāgniś ca prāṇād vāyur ajāyata ||
english: The moon was born from his mind; the sun was born from his eye. From his mouth came Indra and Agni; from his breath Vāyu was born.

sanskrit: nābhyā āsīd antarikṣaṁ śīrṣṇo dyauḥ sam avartata | padbhyāṁ bhūmir diśaḥ śrotrāt tathā lokām̐ akalpayan ||
english: From his navel came the atmosphere; from his head the sky evolved. From his two feet the earth; from his ear the directions — thus they arranged the worlds.

sanskrit: saptāsyāsan paridhayaḥ triḥ sapta samidhaḥ kṛtāḥ | devā yad yajñaṁ tanvānā abadhnan puruṣam paśum ||
english: Seven were its enclosing sticks; thrice seven were the kindling-sticks prepared, when the gods, spreading out the sacrifice, bound the Puruṣa as the sacrificial animal.

sanskrit: yajñena yajñam ayajanta devās tāni dharmāṇi prathamāny āsan | te ha nākam mahimānaḥ sacanta yatra pūrve sādhyāḥ santi devāḥ ||
english: With the sacrifice the gods sacrificed to the sacrifice; these were the first cosmic laws. These great ones attained the vault of heaven, where the ancient Sādhya gods dwell.
